TX.name: Texas
policy: Aug 3: Gov. Abbott ordered a PUC/ERCOT audit of every data center in the interconnection queue; ERCOT paused Batch Zero. Projects that fail the audit 'must be denied' connection.

Sep 21: Abbott ordered TCEQ to pause all data-center-related environmental permits, including behind-the-meter gas generation. TCEQ compliance report due Oct 19; pause runs until ERCOT review ends (~mid-Dec).
ERCOT large-load queue ~474 GW, ~90% data centers. BofA: ~50 GW of the ~253 GW U.S. pipeline could be affected.
Only 20 of 138 sales-tax-exempt facilities have finished compliance audits ($3.3B in exemptions). Bill pre-filing opens Nov 9; 60+ data center bills expected.

race.rating: Likely R (Cook) but polling within 2 pts
positions: Abbott (R): backed the 2015 sales-tax exemptions; pivoted in Aug to case-by-case audits and grid oversight.
Hinojosa (D): wants a special session to repeal the exemptions and a pause on new projects until guardrails exist.

TX.extra: Senate: Talarico (D) 45 / Paxton (R) 45 (UMass Lowell, Sep 18-28). Voters: 65% oppose an AI data center in their community; 56% back a statewide ban on new builds (UMass Lowell).
TX.implication: Either outcome keeps the audit gate on un-energized ERCOT loads into 1H27. A Hinojosa win adds tax-exemption repeal risk, which hits project economics for every Texas lease underwritten on exempt equipment purchases. Behind-the-meter gas projects lost their workaround on Sep 21.

NY.name: New York
policy: Jul 14: EO 62, the first statewide moratorium. One-year pause on new state environmental permits for facilities over 50 MW. Existing operations and fully permitted expansions continue.
Hochul also wants to ban tax breaks for data centers. Local pauses: Town of Tonawanda, Mohawk, East Greenbush, Clay.

positions: Hochul (D): signed the moratorium; running on it.

NY.implication: Hochul's re-election locks in the moratorium through mid-2027. Permitted Lake Mariner buildings continue; any new campus or unpermitted expansion (Lake Hawkeye/Cayuga) is frozen.

MI.name: Michigan
policy: Moratorium bills HB 5594-5596 in committee; Gov. Whitmer opposes them.
63 local actions, including Flint (12 mo), Lansing (182 days), Ypsilanti Twp (180 days). Augusta Twp voters overturned a rezoning.
Saline Twp first tried to block the Stargate campus, then settled after lawsuits. The MPSC-approved DTE contract carries consumer protections; both parties want them written into state law.

positions: Both nominees call for a moratorium on new projects while rules are written.
Benson (D): statewide pause; her husband works for Related Cos., Saline's developer (says he has stepped away from Michigan projects).
James (R): local control, industrial land over farmland, blames state tax breaks.

MI.extra: Senate (open): El-Sayed (D) plan says no rate hikes, data centers pay for their own energy.
MI.implication: Whoever wins, the next governor backs a pause on new builds. Saline is under construction with an approved DTE contract, so it is most likely grandfathered, but later phases and any new Michigan site face a moratorium and codified ratepayer terms.

WI.name: Wisconsin
policy: PSC ruling could force Oracle to post $7B+ of collateral for We Energies plant and line costs at Port Washington; Oracle sued and offered ~$700M (10%).
Marquette: 70% say data center costs outweigh benefits, up from 55% six months earlier. 7 projects worth $57B pending.
Local pauses: Madison, Superior, Oshkosh, Manitowoc Co.; Wrightstown voters rejected a project.

positions: Tiffany (R): no new data centers unless standards are met, end state subsidies, local veto, no farmland conversion. Ad brands his opponent 'Data Center David Crowley'.
Crowley (D): opposes a statewide moratorium; wants guardrails and incentives tied to jobs. Both want an NDA ban and developers paying grid upgrades.

WI.implication: Unusual case where the Republican is the more restrictive candidate. A Tiffany win raises the odds that the PSC collateral stands and that subsidies end, both bad for Port Washington economics.

GA.name: Georgia
policy: No statewide law; 8 state bills failed or pending.
Local pauses: Savannah and Chatham Co. (155 days), Americus; Fayetteville banned; Atlanta Beltline area prohibited.
Two of five PSC seats on the Nov 3 ballot; Democrats need both to flip the 3-2 GOP majority that sets Georgia Power large-load rates.

positions: Democratic side has called for a moratorium on new construction (BofA, Oct 5).
Jackson (R): avg lead 0.9 pts across four pollsters.

GA.implication: A Bottoms win plus a PSC flip would reopen large-load cost allocation (BofA flags Southern Co.). That is the main risk to un-energized Georgia builds like Sandersville and the Dalton expansion.

OH.name: Ohio
policy: Gov. DeWine paused new tax-exemption requests (May 27); SB 646 pending.
55 local moratoriums; 21 local ballot measures on Nov 3.
AEP Ohio already has an approved large-load tariff.

positions: Ramaswamy (R): moratorium; make operators pay nearby residents' power bills.

OH.implication: No focus-desk collateral in Ohio, but it is the clearest sign that restriction is now bipartisan: both nominees run on a pause.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
policy: Aug 18: Gov. Shapiro's EO 2026-05 sets GRID requirements for 25 MW+ and removes fast-track permitting.
HB 2496 (lets municipalities pause projects) passed the House 201-1.
BofA: key variables are allowed ROE and large-load pricing reviews.

positions: Shapiro (D): pro-build with cost and grid standards.

PA.implication: Policy continuity is near certain. Risk is local: if HB 2496 becomes law, townships gain pause authority over sites without final approvals.

NJ.name: New Jersey
policy: Jul 7: Fair Share Act. Operators of 50 MW+ must commit to 85% of projected power costs for 10 years.
Aug 28: energy and water reporting law.
93 municipal bans (Bayonne, Cherry Hill, Medford, Millville, Monroe Twp).
NJ.implication: No 2026 statewide race. The cost has already moved to operators: take-or-pay power commitments raise fixed costs for Vineland and Kenilworth.

VA.name: Virginia
policy: Sep 18: Gov. Spanberger's EO 22 ends by-right zoning for 25 MW+.
$0.011/kWh data center tax enacted; 60+ bills tracked. Loudoun Co. ended by-right zoning.
VA.implication: No 2026 governor race (Spanberger elected 2025). Projects already zoned and under construction are mostly insulated; new sites face discretionary review.

IL.name: Illinois
policy: Tax-incentive pause since Jul 1, indefinite.
Local: Lawrence Co. (2 yr), Champaign Co., Mattoon; Chicago ordinance pending.
IL.implication: Continuity. Pressure falls on project economics through lost incentives rather than outright bans; the Elk Grove cluster already has power.

NM.name: New Mexico
policy: Project Jupiter faces public-records and permit litigation; a June suit was dismissed with leave to refile.
Statewide moratorium proposed for the 2027 session. Local pauses: Rio Communities, Colfax Co.
NM.implication: A Haaland administration sets the tone for the 2027 moratorium debate while Jupiter's off-grid gas and fuel-cell microgrid still needs air permits.

LA.name: Louisiana
policy: Jun 25: Gov. Landry's EO 26-058 requires full infrastructure funding before tax incentives.
Entergy Louisiana building 3 GW of new gas generation for Hyperion. New Orleans interim zoning only.
LA.implication: No 2026 governor race. The most supportive state on the map; the main risk is construction and cost, not politics.

ND.name: North Dakota
policy: No statewide restrictions.
7 local moratoriums near Applied Digital's Polaris Forge campuses; annexation fight around Harwood.
ND.implication: No 2026 governor race. State policy is supportive; watch county pauses around expansion parcels.

OK.name: Oklahoma
policy: Oklahoma City moratorium through Dec 31, 2026.
SB 1488 statewide bill in committee; HB 2992 ratepayer protection signed.
OK.implication: Low election risk. BofA lists Oklahoma among states where a Democratic upset would carry policy risk, but no public polling shows one.

KY.name: Kentucky
policy: Aug 6: Gov. Beshear's EO directs permit denials for harmful impacts and bars utility rate increases tied to data centers.
Woodford Co. permanent ban; Louisville Metro 6-month; Lexington-Fayette pause.
KY.implication: No 2026 governor race (next is 2027). The EO puts the burden on Hawesville to prove no rate impact on other customers.

NC.name: North Carolina
policy: Jul 7: restrictions on certified data centers signed; H 1189 (2-year pause for 100 MW+) in committee.
Local pauses in 14 counties and 25+ towns: Charlotte, Greensboro, Cary, Durham.
NC.implication: No 2026 governor race. Operating sites are fine; new 100 MW+ builds face local and possible statewide pauses.

AL.name: Alabama
policy: SB 270 (PSC review) pending.
Local 6-month pauses in Leeds, Homewood, Springville, Chelsea, Westover.

MO.name: Missouri
policy: No statewide action. Jackson Co. 180-day moratorium; St. Charles city ban; Springfield 120-day.
Independence plans to rebuild a retired municipal plant to serve the Nebius campus.
MO.implication: No 2026 governor race. Risk sits in Jackson County politics and power-plant execution.

WA.name: Washington
policy: ESSB 6231 phases out the sales-tax exemption.
Local pauses: Seattle, Spokane, Snohomish Co., Skagit.
WA.implication: No 2026 governor race. Economics, not bans.

AZ.name: Arizona
policy: Tax-incentive pause since Jun 13.
Tucson siting limits for 20 MW+; Pima Co. 120-day.
AZ.implication: No focus-desk collateral. BofA thinks the market overstates election risk here.

flags.title: Oracle force majeure: Project Jupiter (NM)
flags.body: Oracle sent a force majeure notice to the developer. If the power delay qualifies, Oracle can defer full rent for up to 3 years past the 2028 target, paying only development-stage rent and part of interest in the meantime. Cause: the Green Chile gas pipeline slipped to Feb 1, 2027 after two State Land Office right-of-way denials, and the fuel-cell air permit is stalled after the NM Supreme Court paused proceedings. The construction loan was quoted at ~89-91. Not an event of default.

flags.title: Same fact pattern: Vantage Frontier (TX)
flags.body: Frontier also runs on behind-the-meter gas. Texas's TCEQ permit pause blocks new air permits until the ERCOT audit ends (~mid-Dec). A Jupiter-style force majeure notice would be the obvious next step if the microgrid slips.

flags.title: Port Washington collateral fight (WI)
flags.body: Wisconsin PSC ruling could force Oracle to post $7B+ of collateral for dedicated plant and lines. Oracle sued and offered ~$700M. Oracle was cut to BBB- on Jul 9, the level that triggers stricter collateral rules.

flags.title: Riot bridge matures before rent
flags.body: Interim facility matures about a year before the first 96 MW starts paying rent (Dec 2027). The investment-grade credit backstop for the $1.7-2.1B takeout is not finalized.

flags.title: TeraWulf Hawesville bridge and takeout
flags.body: $3.5B HY/loan takeout launched Jul 2026, not closed. Power is now contracted (KY PSC approved a 482 MW Big Rivers/Kenergy contract Aug 21), but the bridge matures before first rent in 2H27 and Kentucky's Aug 6 executive order puts all cost on the operator.

flags.title: Backstops start only at rent commencement
flags.body: Cipher's 10-Q says tenant guarantees and backstops take effect only after rent commencement and are capped or limited by default triggers. Until a hall commences, a delivery delay sits with the landlord and its bondholders, not Google.

flags.title: CleanSpark: milestone-based abatement or termination
flags.body: Missed milestones can trigger rent abatement or lease termination. The site has run as a mining campus since 2022, but the added AI load and utility are not disclosed, and Georgia's governor race and two PSC seats are toss-ups.

flags.title: CoreWeave: $35.5B of leases not yet commenced
flags.body: Per the Q2 10-Q, 748 MW across sites was undelivered at Jun 30, phasing through 2028. Applied Digital's Bldg 4 lease moves to a CoreWeave subsidiary only once that subsidiary is investment grade.

flags.title: Oracle: $288B of leases not yet commenced
flags.body: Per the Aug 31, 2026 10-Q, substantially all data center leases with 15-19 year terms, not on the balance sheet. A Jupiter-style deferral right across these leases would shift timing risk to landlords and lenders.
